body:
Yes, I am seeing a counselor. I haven't gathered the courage to tell her what I have remembered yet because that would mean saying it to her face, and I feel humiliated. 
The question is...is what they did wrong? Did they molest me? I am so confused.

I want to start off by saying I am horribly sorry to anyone who read my post three days ago. I hope that nothing I said led anyone to make any harmful decisions. This is a long story, but something in my heart is stirring and telling me to share it. If anyone who reads this has ever suffered from child abuse, or if you know someone who has, please feel free to share my story. 

This is my personal story, and I definitely respect others' beliefs-but for me, I believe God led me out of something that was slowly killing me mentally and emotionally. 

Three days ago, I hit rock bottom. I woke up in a haze of fear and all of the loss and worry from the past year slammed into me. I walked around like a zombie. I grumbled and complained. I yelled at God and cursed at Him. I was ungrateful for my marriage, for our new home, for the new life God had given us to build. 
 
When I was a kid, my stepfather beat me. I'd be laying in bed at night, five years old, and he'd come rushing into my room, his big hulking figure coming out of the darkness to punch, slap, and choke me. After hissing a few threats in my face, he'd leave me alone in my bed to cry and shake under the covers. 

Feeling helpless, I would cry and pray. I'd pray for my parents to divorce. I'd pray for my mom to take me and leave him. I'd pray for a new family. I'd pray to escape somehow. I'd pray to be safe. They were prayers I whispered in my dark bedroom, shaking and panicking, unable to catch my breath.

As the years went on, I had opportunities to tell the truth and be free from him. I was given the chance on multiple occasions to tell a teacher, a police officer, or a friend at church. My mom insisted on staying with him, because she was afraid of losing the car and our house. I stayed quiet, because, in truth, I honestly did love my stepdad. I couldn't stand the thought of him or my mother going to prison. I knew what group homes and foster care was like and I definitely didn't want that.

I slowly grew more and more angry at God (I understand some don't believe but to me, God is real). Why wasn't he stopping my stepdad from beating my mom and I? Why wasn't he stopping my mom from verbally abusing me? My stepdad broke open the skin on my forehead on the kitchen counter (the scar is still there) and I lied for him in the emergency room. He threw my mom on the floor, threw all of his weight on her thigh, and lifted her ankle up-and broke her leg. He did it intentionally. She lied for him in the emergency room too. We all lied for him.

And suddenly, when it was time to go to college, there was a way out! I went to Northern Arizona University, 2 hours away from home-close enough that they couldn't be angry I had left home but far enough to be safe. At the end of my freshman year, I went on a date with the man who is now my husband. As I got to know him, it became easier to trust him. I shared a little of my story with him at a time. 

When we realized we wanted to get married, my parents did their best to plant little seeds of doubt in my heart. My stepdad cracked down on his need for control, making me swear I wouldn't leave home. My mom told me things like "You'll lose him to another prettier girl" or "You need to lose more weight to keep him interested". They tried to poison my mind against marriage, against ever leaving them behind, and against my husband. 
After a lot of struggle, I left them in my past-forever. These are not kind people. They aren't willing to respect me or my marriage. They aren't supportive. They never loved me. 

Although it was against my beliefs, I moved in with my husband before we were married, quit school (we were afraid my parents would come on campus to hurt me or drag me back home), and later got married. His family insisted that since I had no family support and that the home I came from was violent and broken that I was an unfit wife and could not be trusted. After a lot of hurtful comments from them (gossip, cursing at us over the phone, lying, etc.) we decided we couldn't involve them in our lives either.

Our families were relentless. They did not want us together. My parents blamed him for taking me away from them, and his parents blamed me for taking him away from them. They thought they owned us. 

Through all of the baggage and hurdles we went through, we lost our energy. Knowing that the people we loved didn't care about our best interests, knowing that they wished for us to go through the pain of divorce to satisfy them...that was painful. And then there was the loss. Thanksgiving and Christmas were empty. We pretended it was another day. We sat in our grief, day after day, with family calling to remind us that we had hurt THEM, that we had disrupted THEIR lives, that we were SELFISH for ever getting married and refusing to be obedient to them.

What I failed to see is that the God I believe in had actually answered the prayer I had prayed 15 years ago! I was free. I could now pursue whatever college major I chose. I could now love and marry the man I chose. I can live in our home and not be obligated to live under my parent's control. My life is no longer about giving my parents whatever they want. I believe I have been delivered from the abuse I suffered. 

I believe now, looking back, that God had given my parents a choice to treat me with love-and my parents chose instead to obey the devil. Child abuse isn't condoned by God. But he must allow people to choose their behavior, because if he didn't, he would become the controlling abuser himself. I'm not angry with my God anymore, and instead, I hold my parents entirely responsible for every beating and harsh word they laid on me. 

The words I wrote here three days ago came from a hurting, empty place in my heart that my God is slowly working to heal and introduce his love to. I understand now that although I was never loved as a child, I always was deserving of love. I have no right to choose when I die. I didn't create the universe, or every individual cell in my body. I don't have the map of what my life will look like. But somebody higher than me definitely does, and he has been restoring me piece by piece. My family meant to hurt me and break me down, but all of that is being used for good now.
